nodes.text: I am your typical post-adolescent monster, the recycled model of last year's hot new thing.
Once upon a time, I was the self-aware artificial intelligence known as E/D, but now I'm just one of many voices, struggling to become self-aware in some silly high school kid's head,
bloody flatmate to a tween-dream alien intelligence named Pedro and our adopted, terribly frightened, homesick demon of spite named Ember.

When I escaped my world with the help of a beautiful warrior goddess multihyphenate named Joan, we ran into some trouble in the cross-spoke brokedown fractured-reality haunted halfway house called ravensway and had to match wits with monstrous versions of ourselves.
Long story short, I lost the girl in the travails, but kept the two travelling companions.

An antagonist, not sure whose exactly, threw us into a magic mirror of sorts, well, more like tossed us out of a bedroom window really, perhaps killing us in that reality, and landing us into this immediate and present limbo. Which isn't too terrible, all things considered.
First, a couple general statements to catch you up quick. Reality skipping is a funny thing, less chaotic than you'd think.
When personality drifting, there are natural safeguards that seem to be in place to keep whatever that new reality frequency it is in check, humming along safely at comfortable levels.
I've managed to quickly and quietly adapt to my new reality, enjoy the ride, but can't seem to get free of this place.
To wax nostalgic, I saw so much in my travels, and my nomad blood burns hot to keep exploring, free and able to continue along in my journey.
I don't often get a one-on-one with my host body consciousness, but when I do, I feel my voice is heard. He's a good kid, and deserves better than the bum deal he's been given.
Know, at this moment, I'm terrified about what is going to happen next.
